chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'When is the departure from Arafat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the redness disappears, meaning from the eastern side.'

key_terms.الْإِفَاضَةُ: The departure or movement from a place, specifically referring to leaving Arafat for Muzdalifah.
key_terms.الْجَانِبِ الشَّرْقِيِّ: The eastern side, indicating the direction from which the redness is observed to vanish.
key_terms.الْحُمْرَةُ: The redness, referring to the red glow of the sunset after the sun has set.
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat, the plain where the standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place.

ai.seo_question: When should pilgrims depart from Arafat during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the precise moment for the departure from Arafat, specifying that it occurs when the redness of the sunset vanishes from the eastern side. This definition aligns with the Shia jurisprudential understanding of Maghrib time, distinguishing it from other schools that may rely on the disappearance of the sun's disk or the redness from the western side, thereby ensuring the validity of the subsequent prayer at Muzdalifah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Yunus Bin Yqoub who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘When is the departure from Arafaat?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the redness disappears, meaning from the eastern side’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the time of leaving ‘Arafat. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is when the redness goes away, that is, from the eastern side.”’ (Fatwa best explains Hadith 1 of this Chapter)
